_comment: Project-scoped MCP servers. Checked into git so this repo always talks to the
Opportunity Outdoors accounts, never whichever account happens to be authorized
globally on the machine. Project scope beats user scope, so these override any
No credentials live here. Each server shells out to read its key from ./.env.local,
which is gitignored, so the config is shareable and the secrets stay local.
SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN  personal access token from the account owning ffivubkouyqzvebuxflf
On the stripe server: it reads STRIPE_MCP_KEY, deliberately NOT the STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
the app itself uses. The app needs write access to create checkout sessions; an agent
driving this server does not, and keeping them separate means one can be narrowed
without breaking the other. Put a TEST MODE restricted key here (rk_test_...). Stripe
derives tool permissions from the key, so the key IS the sandbox: a read-only test key
cannot move money regardless of what any tool asks for. Never put sk_live_ in this slot.
Create one at https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/apikeys under Restricted keys.

args: if [ -f ./.env.local ]; then export SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN="$(grep -E '^SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=' ./.env.local | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//')"; fi; exec npx -y @supabase/mcp-server-supabase@latest --project-ref=ffivubkouyqzvebuxflf
if [ -f ./.env.local ]; then export RESEND_API_KEY="$(grep -E '^RESEND_API_KEY=' ./.env.local | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//')"; fi; exec npx -y resend-mcp
if [ -f ./.env.local ]; then export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="$(grep -E '^STRIPE_MCP_KEY=' ./.env.local | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//')"; fi; exec npx -y @stripe/mcp --tools=all
